title: Quarterly decision calendar and alignment playbook for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Create a repeatable quarterly decision calendar and playbook that synchronizes Hosted API product priorities with the Model Catalog curation cycle. Background: We have quarterly model rotations, canary windows, and SLA-sensitive customers that require a predictable decision rhythm. This ticket scopes the calendar, stakeholder forum cadence (PM/ENG/Design/Trust), gating criteria for model promotion/deprecation, and a lightweight audit trail for release decisions. Deliverables: 1) a shared calendar template (Confluence) with decision milestones; 2) a prioritized checklist for model onboarding/offboarding tied to evaluation pass/fail gates; 3) an operational playbook for canary rollouts and rollback criteria; 4) a tracker dashboard with OKR mapping for the quarter.
acceptance_criteria: A calendar template with milestone definitions (decision freeze, canary start/end, broad rollback window) exists in Confluence and is linked in the product plan.
A gating checklist for model promotion that includes perf/latency benchmarks, regression eval pass rate, and cost delta is documented and has owner assignments.
A stakeholder cadence (weekly sync + decision day in week 6) is scheduled and recurring invites are created.
A lightweight dashboard (Grafana/Console) surfaces model health + canary metrics and is referenced in the playbook.
Signoff flow defined: who approves a model promotion/deprecation and who triggers a rollback.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Eng Leads (runtime, infra) and Research. Agreed to baseline canary window at 72 hours for minor model changes and 7 days for major architecture changes. Action: ENG to document canary metric set (latency p95, token cost delta, hallucination regression rate).

risks: Timing mismatch with Dedicated capacity commit windows could force model holdbacks; mitigation: surface Dedicated customer commit windows in calendar and create fallback model variants.
Insufficient eval coverage may allow regressions to slip into hosted; mitigation: require an eval pass and threshold for all promoted models and run a synthetic smoke suite during canary.
Operational load during overlapping rollouts (multiple models same week); mitigation: cap concurrent promotions and use a priority queue in the cadence playbook.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week -2 to 0): Feature freeze and prep — finalize model candidate list and run pre-canary evaluations.
Phase 1 (Week 1): Canary rollouts to 5% traffic with monitoring hooks for latency, error rate, and quality regressions.
Phase 2 (Week 2-3): Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% if no regression signals; run nightly regression evals against canary traffic samples.
Phase 3 (Week 4): Full production promotion if all gates pass; schedule post-promote review and mark OKR mapping.
Rollback policy: automatic rollback on sustained latency p95 increase >15% for 60 minutes or quality regression rate >2% for 24 hours; manual rollback triggers documented and owner assigned.
decisions: Adopted a 3-tier model promotion gate: (1) automated eval pass, (2) runtime perf within threshold, (3) security/compliance signoff for Private customers.
Set default canary window to 72 hours for minor changes, extendable to 7 days for architecture changes per Eng recommendation.
Require a post-mortem for any promotion that is rolled back within 30 days.
notes: This playbook intentionally keeps the decision body small (PM, Eng lead, Research) to avoid calendar stalls; broader stakeholder notifications happen at decision day.
Tie the decisions back to team OKRs: reduce hosted API token-cost variance by 10% (OKR-3) and maintain p95 latency SLO for interactive models (OKR-1).
Next steps: finalize template, automate checklist enforcement in GitHub issue template, and run a dry-run with a low-risk model in Cycle 41.
